content_metadata.description: An informative video guide teaching viewers how to assemble their personal first aid kits, making them better than standard first aid kits.

qAndA.answer: The narrator recommends using a sharpie instead of a pencil because sharpies are easier to see, don't poke holes in ziploc bags, and you don't need to sharpen them.
qAndA.question: Why does the narrator recommend using a Sharpie instead of a pencil?

qAndA.answer: The narrator recommends ditching the scissors because he thinks anyone going on a camping or hiking trip should have a knife or multitool, and these should have some sort of cutting implement on them anyway, rendering the scissors redundant.
qAndA.question: Why does the narrator recommend ditching the scissors?

qAndA.answer: You should check with an adult before taking any medication, like Tylenol or Ibuprofen, on a camping trip.
qAndA.question: What should you check with an adult before taking on a camping trip?

qAndA.answer: The narrator recommends taking duct tape because it is a cheap and effective alternative to moleskin. He cautions viewers that some people get rashes from duct tape, so they should test it out on their skin before taking it on a trip.
qAndA.question: Why does the narrator recommend taking duct tape, and what caution does he give about it?

qAndA.answer: The narrator emphasizes that first aid kits are 'situational' because what is needed in a first aid kit may vary depending on the type of activity, the duration of the activity, and who is going to be using it.
qAndA.question: Why does the narrator emphasize that first aid kits are 'situational'?

narrativeProgression.description: The narrator shows viewers a Boy Scout first aid manual that has a list of recommended items for a personal first aid kit.
The narrator shows each of the items from the recommended list.
The narrator recommends that instead of taking an entire roll of medical tape, the viewers fold a length of tape, making it smaller and easier to pack.
The narrator recommends that instead of using a pencil, viewers use a sharpie. He explains why this is a good idea.
The narrator recommends ditching the scissors as viewers should have a knife with a cutting implement on it with them anyway.
The narrator recommends taking Tylenol or Ibuprofen, but reminds viewers to check with an adult before taking any medication on a trip.
The narrator recommends taking a length of duct tape as an alternative to moleskin.
The narrator cautions viewers that some people get rashes from duct tape and recommends testing it before taking it on a trip.
The narrator shows an on-screen checklist of all recommended items for a first aid kit.
The narrator emphasizes that first aid kits are situational and viewers may need to make adjustments depending on the activity and duration of the trip.
